comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Two shapes the adapter has to absorb, from the 0.8.0 observation pass:

The API socket is connection-per-request - herdr answers and closes, so the adapter cannot hold one channel for intents. Only events.subscribe persists, and subscribing replays the current session as synthetic events, so a client that snapshots then subscribes sees every entity twice.

Event names are spelled two ways. Most arrive snake_cased (pane_created, tab_focused); the three parameterized subscriptions keep their dotted names in the event (pane.agent_status_changed, pane.output_matched, pane.scroll_changed). The corpus recorder silently returned an empty result over this before it was caught, which is exactly the failure the contract tier exists to prevent.

creator: Alexander Terp
description: The core speaks a Muster-owned contract - pane tree, pane byte streams, agent states, intents - and everything herdr-shaped lives in a single adapter module. The contract corpus doubles as the spec any replacement backend (fork or wholesale) must pass. Exit lanes and rationale: docs/origin.md, 'The decision'.
title: Define the backend seam: Muster's vocabulary, herdr in one adapter
